title: Relative position scores
goal:
Section 2.1 says the Conformer attention module uses the relative sinusoidal encoding of Transformer-XL. A query at frame $i$ scores a key at frame $j$ with a term that depends on the offset $r = i - j$. The course lesson writes the score for one head as

$$
A_{ij} = \frac{(q_i + u)^\top k_j + (q_i + v)^\top p_{i-j}}{\sqrt{d_k}}
$$

The paper cites Transformer-XL for this form and doesn't write it out, so this equation comes from that work. Here `u` and `v` are learned vectors, and `p_r` is the already-projected encoding of offset `r`.

Write `rel_scores(q, k, p, u, v)`. `q` and `k` have shape `(T, dk)`. `p` has shape `(2T - 1, dk)`, and row `m` holds the encoding for offset `r = T - 1 - m`. So row 0 is offset `T - 1`, the middle row is offset 0, and the last row is offset `-(T - 1)`. `u` and `v` have shape `(dk,)`. Return the `(T, T)` array `A`.
hints: Offset `i - j` lives in row `m = T - 1 - (i - j) = T - 1 - i + j` of `p`.
Compute the content term as `(q + u) @ k.T`, a `(T, T)` array.
Compute `(q + v) @ p.T`, a `(T, 2T - 1)` array whose column `m` scores every query against row `m` of `p`. Then pick the right column for each pair.
Build the pick with index arrays: `idx = (T - 1) - np.arange(T)[:, None] + np.arange(T)[None, :]`, and then `np.take_along_axis(pos, idx, axis=1)`.
